summary.title: Errors, Errors Everywhere: How We Centralized and Structured Error Handling
summary.one_liner: Learn how one team moved from ad hoc Go error messages to a centralized, namespace-coded error framework with wrapping trees, context tags, and mapping to Protobuf, HTTP and gRPC codes.
keywords: how to organize errors in large codebase
takeaways: Go errors are plain values; without a convention, error messages and codes drift apart across packages and developers.
Use namespaced error codes (e.g. PRFL.USR.NOT_FOUND) declared in one place, and have each layer wrap dependency errors with its own code.
Build errors as a tree of wrapped codes, attach key/value tags and context, and expose only the top-level code across service boundaries.
Map internal codes automatically to Protobuf ErrorCode/ErrorType, HTTP and gRPC status, and logging/metric tags to keep external APIs backward compatible.
summary.summary:
The author describes a team's journey from simple Go error wrapping with pkg/errors and exported error variables to a structured, centralized error framework. Problems included scattered error declarations, inconsistent log messages, lost context, and no categorization for monitoring. The proposed design uses namespace codes such as DEPS.PG.NOT_FOUND and PRFL.USR.NOT_FOUND, where each layer wraps lower-level errors with its own code, forming a tree. The article walks through the connectly.ai package layout, the Error interface with Error0, VlError and ApiError types, and example code for creating, wrapping, tagging and mapping errors.</summary>
